title: Measure bounded destination write overlap in Chromium
question: Does one in-flight destination write save time in addition to removing the copy and coalescing writes?
summary: A single in-flight write repeatedly helped plain streaming to OPFS. Coalescing accounted for most of the gain and combining the two further reduced whole-job time. Preserve normal publication until desktop selection and production buffer accounting are qualified.

workloads: Direct browser CSV and gzip streaming and eight-key partition output to same-origin OPFS.

validation.summary: Verified 48 screen jobs and eight disk-backed jobs. Direct, async and combined worker variants each passed eight marker, failure, and cancellation cases.

limitations: One headless Chromium build on WSL and one destination model in this experiment.
The prototype owns up to two additional 1 MiB buffers outside WASI working reservations.
exclusions: User-selected-folder speed claims, sustained device throughput, and default promotion.
reopen_when: Repeat the comparison with picker-selected output and qualify browser buffer ownership and end-to-end failure controls.
